question: Some agricultural agreements between the EU and third countries are reportedly aimed at the expansion of certain fruit varieties, with the EU incentivising cultivation of those varieties by allocating financial resources. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the fact that the European Union is financing the expansion of fruit growing in non-EU countries through direct or indirect funding?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.6.2024) In 2022 the value of fruit and vegetables produced in the EU was estimated at EUR 73.4 billion, more than 14% of all agricultural production. The EU is the world’s number one agri-food exporter.

At the same time, the EU is traditionally a net importer of fruit and vegetables, mainly tropical fruits and counter-seasonal produce to ensure year-long supply for European consumers. Fruit and nuts represent approximately 23% of agricultural imports from Africa, an important source of revenue for millions of smallholder farmers in the continent.
EU international cooperation has provided a long-standing support to sustainable agriculture, forestry and fisheries in developing countries as well as in enlargement and neighbourhood regions.

This area of cooperation is included in the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument – Global Europe (NDICI-GE, see Annex II)1 for the period 2021-2027 as well as in the Instrument for pre-accession assistance (IPA), whereby the EU supports the alignment of candidate countries and potential candidates with the EU agricultural policy.

As such, the EU funded several actions in support of fruit and horticulture production, processing and commercialisation in third countries with the objective to increase food security, create economic opportunities and jobs. In parallel, the EU remains committed to preserving the EU agriculture livelihood.

This is why the EU’s approach to negotiations of trade agreements seeks to guarantee adequate protection for EU sensitive products through limited market openings, such as bananas, and to maintaining certain tariffs for fruit categories produced in the EU on a seasonal basis.
